scope_note: This file covers the four engines assigned to this group: Google, Bing, Yahoo, Yandex. The other engines named in the user's request (Startpage, Ecosia, Qwant, Mojeek, Baidu, Naver, SearXNG) are not covered here.
policy: Search result pages are canonical pages: keep only parameters that change which results are shown; remove everything else by default. Preserve parameter order and raw percent-encoding of kept values.
method: Primary sources first: Google XML API reference and the live advanced-search forms; Bing Web Search API docs and live bing.com links; Yahoo preferences form; Yandex Search API docs; SearXNG engine modules; Chromium prepopulated_engines.json, its schema and template_url.cc; Firefox search-config-v2; ClearURLs and AdGuard URL Tracking rules. Secondary: SerpApi's open-source SDK, surfraw, yandex-images-download, Oxylabs, SEO articles. Anything without a source is marked inferred.
cross_engine_conflicts: Yandex lr: functional (region ranking) per Yandex docs, but stripped by ClearURLs and auto-added from IP geolocation by Yandex (location leak).
Google gs_ssp: Chromium treats it as canonical search intent; ClearURLs strips all gs_*.
Google ie: ClearURLs strips it; AdGuard disabled its ie rule because it breaks non-UTF-8 queries. Keep when not UTF-8.
Bing FORM: ClearURLs strips form; AdGuard commented out its FORM rule after a breakage report (issue 215377) tied to in-browser rewriting; old SearXNG sent FORM=PERE to stabilise automated paging.
Location-revealing but functional: Google uule (and to a lesser degree gl/hl), Yandex lr/rstr.

hosts: www.google.<tld> and google.<tld> for every Google ccTLD (google.com, google.co.uk, google.no, google.com.br ...); match ^(www\.)?google\.(com|[a-z]{2,3}|co\.[a-z]{2}|com\.[a-z]{2})$ (ClearURLs uses (?:[a-z0-9-]+\.)*?google(?:\.[a-z]{2,}){1,})
paths: /search (all verticals: web, tbm=/udm= images, videos, news, shopping, books, local)
/webhp, / and /search with the query in the fragment (#q=...) and /s?q=... (Chromium alternate_urls)
Not result pages, unwrap instead: /url?q= or /url?url= (redirect), /aclk (ad click, ClearURLs leaves it alone), /amp/s/<url>

engines.notes: the owner's test (https://www.google.com/search?q=bag&... -> ?q=bag) already passes and matches test 1. Rule of thumb: keep q, start, num, tbm, udm, hl, gl, lr, cr, safe, tbs, filter, nfpr, pws, every as_*, the img* image filters, ijn, si, gs_ssp, kgmid, uule, ludocid, lsig, ibp, htidocid, and ie only when not UTF-8; drop everything else. Do not use a blanket gs_* strip without exempting gs_ssp. Fragments: #imgrc=, #vhid=, #lrd= select an item inside the result page (inferred); #q= carries the query on /webhp and / (Chromium alternate_urls). Google Lens result pages (/search?vsrid=...&lns_mode=...&udm=26) depend on session ids and cannot be canonicalised (inferred); leave them alone or warn. ClearURLs also strips 'site' and 'ie' unconditionally on Google; 'site' is not a /search parameter (use the site: operator or as_sitesearch), and 'ie' is handled conditionally here. Related products with their own functional sets, out of scope here: news.google.com (hl, gl, ceid are functional; ClearURLs exempts news.google.com hl) and scholar.google.com (q, start, hl, as_sdt, as_vis, as_ylo, as_yhi per SearXNG google_scholar.py).

engines.notes: the owner's test is test 1. Preserve the raw encoding of qft and filters (qft uses + as a literal separator and filters carries quoted values); never re-encode. SearXNG's old engine sent FORM=PERE/PERE<n> with first because automated paging was unreliable without it, and AdGuard commented out '$removeparam=FORM,domain=bing.com' after issue 215377 (blank pages when stripping in-browser). For an offline cleaner the URL is loaded once, so dropping FORM is expected to be fine; verify paging with first=11 alone in a browser. Bing's live news links use interval="4" for past hour, so SearXNG's mapping of 'day' to interval="4" looks wrong (not CheckLink's concern). The API-only names (offset, freshness, safeSearch, responseFilter, answerCount, promote, textDecorations, textFormat) are Bing Web Search API v7 parameters, not bing.com URL parameters; treat them as unknown (dropped). Visual-search pages (/images/search?view=detailv2&iss=sbi or &cbir=sbi&imgurl=...) depend on an uploaded image and are not canonicalisable (inferred).

engines.notes: Strip ;_ylt=/;_ylu=/;_ylc= path segments before query processing (they sit between the path and '?'). Yahoo now gates search behind a YBV cookie (SearXNG) and TLS fingerprinting, so automated verification of these rules failed from curl on 2026-10-10; the SerpApi field names were cross-checked against SearXNG where they overlap (p, b, vm, vl, fl). Secondary sources disagree in places (DataForSEO claims tbs=qdr: and vm=0/1 for Yahoo; not adopted). Yahoo! JAPAN (search.yahoo.co.jp) is a different engine: p query, ei encoding (conditional), b offset; fr and frtype are tracking per AdGuard and Firefox (fr=mozff).

functional.meaning: Images: colour (color, gray, red, orange, cyan, yellow, green, blue, violet, white, black).
functional.condition: yandex-images-download sends 'color'; 'icolor' is the form commonly seen in yandex.* URLs (inferred). Keep both.

functional.name: type / itype
functional.meaning: Images: file type (jpg, png, gifan) and image kind (photo, clipart, lineart, face, demotivator).
functional.condition: Which name carries which filter is not independently verified; keep both.

functional.name: recent
functional.meaning: Images: recent=7D (last 7 days).

functional.name: commercial
functional.meaning: Images: commercial=1 (shopping-related images).

functional.name: site
functional.meaning: Images: restrict to a source site.

functional.name: nomisspell
functional.meaning: Images: 1 disables spelling correction.

functional.name: rpt / url / cbir_id
functional.meaning: Reverse image search: rpt=imageview with url= (or an uploaded image's cbir_id) shows results for that image.
functional.condition: cbir_id inferred.

functional.name: duration / hd
functional.meaning: Videos: duration (short, medium, long) and HD-only.
functional.condition: Names taken from SerpApi; may be SerpApi-level aliases (inferred).

functional.name: searchid
functional.meaning: Site-search widget instance id on /search/site/.
functional.condition: Only on /search/site/.

functional.name: family
functional.meaning: family=yes forces the family (strict) filter.
functional.source: Inferred; Yandex documents the three filter modes as settings only: https://yandex.com/support/search/en/additional-features/adult-filter
functional.condition: Inferred, unverified.

functional.name: noreask
functional.meaning: noreask=1 disables query auto-correction.
functional.condition: Inferred, unverified.

nonfunctional.name: from
nonfunctional.source: Chromium regulatory params from=os&clid=...: https://chromium.googlesource.com/external/search_engines_data/+/refs/heads/main/definitions/prepopulated_engines.json; AdGuard (news, browser): https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/master/TrackParamFilter/sections/specific.txt

nonfunctional.name: win / ncrnd / rdrnd / ui / uuid
nonfunctional.meaning: Partner window id, random nonces and client ids.

nonfunctional.name: tmpl_version / web / frame / search_client
nonfunctional.meaning: Rendering flags of the /search/site/ widget (keep searchid).

nonfunctional.name: sk
nonfunctional.meaning: Signature/CSRF key on some Yandex URLs.
nonfunctional.source: Inferred. AdGuard warns not to strip sk on Yandex Disk (not search): https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/master/TrackParamFilter/sections/specific.txt

engines.notes: Decision needed on lr: test 1 assumes CheckLink keeps it as functional (region). If CheckLink follows ClearURLs on privacy grounds, the expected clean URL becomes https://yandex.ru/search/?text=bag. Note that Yandex re-adds lr from the visitor's own IP on load, so stripping it costs the recipient nothing except the sharer's region choice. AdGuard keeps 'from' removal scoped to news/browser hosts and plain '://yandex.' hosts; on /search/ it is a Chromium-documented attribution code, so drop it there. yandex.com search pages served a CAPTCHA to curl on 2026-10-10, so the image and video filter names rest on open-source clients rather than live pages. Yandex's own help documents filter modes and region only as account settings (yandex.com/tune/search, /tune/geo), not as URL parameters.
